\begin{abstract}
Homotopy $1$-types are modelled faithfully by groupoids: a connected $1$-type with
fundamental group $G$ is modelled by the one-object groupoid $K(G,1)$ whose arrows are the
elements of $G$. The classical unpointed classification asserts that homotopy classes of
maps between connected $1$-types with fundamental groups $G$ and $H$ are in bijection with
$\Hom(G,H)$ modulo conjugation by $H$. The quotient by conjugation is the source of two
structural defects: the classification is functorial only up to conjugacy, and the group of
homotopy self-equivalences of $K(G,1)$ comes out as $\Out(G)$ rather than $\Aut(G)$.

We show that both defects vanish, and that their magnitude is computable exactly, once
basepoints are retained. The technical instrument is a \emph{prescribed-value homotopy
lemma}: for a connected source, any isomorphism $h\colon F(x)\to G(x)$ in the target that
intertwines the two induced fundamental-group actions extends to a homotopy $F\Rightarrow G$
whose component at the basepoint is literally $h$. From it we obtain: the pointed
classification $[(X,x),(Y,y)]_*\cong\Hom(\pi_1(X,x),\pi_1(Y,y))$ for connected $(X,x)$ and

pointed self-equivalence group with $\Aut(G)$; and the exact count
$[H:C_H(\varphi(G))]$ for the fibres of the basepoint-forgetting map, specialising to
$[G:Z(G)]=\lvert\Inn(G)\rvert$ over the identity class and to singletons for abelian
targets. For $G=H=S_3$ the three fibres have sizes $1$, $3$ and $6$.

\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}

The fundamental group is attached not to a space but to a pointed space. For a
path-connected $X$, a path $\gamma$ from $x$ to $x'$ induces an isomorphism
$\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X,x')$, but this isomorphism depends on $\gamma$, and two choices differ
by conjugation. Thus ``the fundamental group of a connected space'' is well defined only up
to a non-canonical isomorphism, and self-comparisons are ambiguous by an inner automorphism.

The ambiguity propagates to the classification of maps. If $X$ and $Y$ are aspherical,
$X\simeq K(G,1)$ and $Y\simeq K(H,1)$, the classical theorem reads
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unpointed}
  [X,Y]\;\cong\;\Hom(G,H)/\text{conjugation by }H.
\end{equation}
Two consequences are structurally unpleasant.

\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Failure of strict functoriality.} The homomorphism induced by a composite
$g\circ f$ is only \emph{conjugate} to $g_\#\circ f_\#$, and the conjugators are
choice-dependent.
\item \emph{$\Out$ instead of $\Aut$.} The monoid of unpointed self-map classes of $K(G,1)$
is the monoid of conjugacy classes of endomorphisms of $G$, whose unit group is
$\Out(G)=\Aut(G)/\Inn(G)$: the inner automorphisms have been quotiented away.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The results}

We work in the groupoid model of $1$-types (Section~\ref{sec:model}). The technical heart is
Theorem~\ref{thm:prescribed}, which strengthens the usual ``conjugate homomorphisms give
homotopic maps'' statement by fixing the value of the homotopy at the basepoint.
Section~\ref{sec:pointed} proves the pointed classification; Section~\ref{sec:strict}
establishes strict functoriality, the endomorphism monoid, the pointed Whitehead theorem and
the pointed self-equivalence group; Section~\ref{sec:fibres} proves the fibre-counting
theorem; Section~\ref{sec:s3} carries out the finite test for $S_3$; Section~\ref{sec:algo}
gives algorithms; Sections~\ref{sec:appl}--\ref{sec:future} discuss applications and open
directions.

\section{The groupoid model of homotopy $1$-types}\label{sec:model}

\begin{definition}[Groupoid]
A \emph{groupoid} is a category in which every morphism is invertible. We write
$\Hom_C(a,b)$ for the arrows $a\to b$ and $\Aut(c)=\Hom_C(c,c)$, the \emph{vertex group}
at $c$.
\end{definition}

The fundamental groupoid $\Pi_1(X)$ has the points of $X$ as objects and homotopy classes rel
endpoints of paths as arrows; it captures precisely the homotopy $1$-type of $X$. We use the
dictionary of Table~\ref{tab:dict} without further comment.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
Topology & Groupoid theory\\
\midrule
homotopy $1$-type $X$ & groupoid $C$\\
point of $X$ & object $c$\\
$\pi_0(X)$ & set of connected components\\
$\pi_1(X,x)$ & vertex group $\Aut(c)$\\

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The dictionary between $1$-types and groupoids.}\label{tab:dict}
\end{table}

\begin{definition}[Connectedness at a basepoint]
A groupoid $C$ is \emph{connected at} $c$ if for every object $X$ there is an isomorphism
$c\to X$. We fix such an arrow $\gamma_X\colon c\to X$ for each $X$, with
$\gamma_c=\mathrm{id}_c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Loop associated with an arrow]
For an arrow $f\colon X\to Y$ set $\ell(f)=\gamma_X\,f\,\gamma_Y^{-1}\in\Aut(c)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The model $K(G,1)$]
For a group $G$ let $\BG G$ be the groupoid with one object $\star$ and
$\Hom(\star,\star)=G$ under multiplication. Every connected $1$-type is equivalent to
$\BG G$ for $G$ its fundamental group.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Realization]\label{prop:realize}
Let $C$ be connected at $c$, let $D$ be a groupoid, $d\in D$, and let
$\varphi\colon\Aut(c)\to\Aut(d)$ be a homomorphism. Then there is a functor
$R_\varphi\colon C\to D$ with $R_\varphi(X)=d$ for all objects $X$ and
$R_\varphi(f)=\varphi(\ell(f))$ for every arrow $f$. In particular $R_\varphi(a)=\varphi(a)$
for $a\in\Aut(c)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Functoriality follows from $\ell(fg)=\ell(f)\ell(g)$ (the chosen arrows cancel in the middle)
and $\ell(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$; apply $\varphi$.
\end{proof}

Note that $R_\varphi$ is constant on objects: this is why the target may be disconnected
without harm.

\section{Homotopies with a prescribed value at the basepoint}

\begin{theorem}[Prescribed-homotopy lemma]\label{thm:prescribed}
Let $C$ be a groupoid connected at $c$, let $D$ be a groupoid, and let $F,G\colon C\to D$ be
functors. Let $h\colon F(c)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }G(c)$ satisfy the intertwining condition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intertwine}
  F(a)\,h \;=\; h\,G(a)\qquad\text{for all }a\in\Aut(c).
\end{equation}
Then there is a natural isomorphism $\eta\colon F\Rightarrow G$ with $\eta_c=h$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define $\eta_X = F(\gamma_X)^{-1}\,h\,G(\gamma_X)\colon F(X)\to G(X)$, an isomorphism. Let
$f\colon X\to Y$ be an arrow and $a=\ell(f)$. Condition~\eqref{eq:intertwine} for $a$ reads
\[
  F(\gamma_X)F(f)F(\gamma_Y)^{-1}\,h \;=\; h\,G(\gamma_X)G(f)G(\gamma_Y)^{-1}.
\]
Pre-composing with $F(\gamma_X)^{-1}$ and post-composing with $G(\gamma_Y)$ yields
$F(f)\,\eta_Y=\eta_X\,G(f)$, the naturality square. Since $\gamma_c=\mathrm{id}_c$ we get
$\eta_c=h$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Condition~\eqref{eq:intertwine} says exactly that conjugation by $h$ carries $a\mapsto F(a)$
to $a\mapsto G(a)$. Standard arguments produce \emph{some} homotopy realizing a conjugacy;
the improvement here is control of its value at the basepoint, and it is precisely this that
makes the pointed theory strict. Connectedness is used only for the source.
\end{remark}

\section{Pointed maps and the pointed classification}\label{sec:pointed}

\begin{definition}[Pointed map]
A \emph{pointed map} $P\colon(C,c)\to(D,d)$ consists of a functor $P^{\mathrm f}\colon C\to D$
and an isomorphism $p\colon P^{\mathrm f}(c)\xrightarrow{\cong}d$, the \emph{chosen path}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Induced homomorphism]
$P_\#\colon\Aut(c)\to\Aut(d)$, $P_\#(a)=p^{-1}P^{\mathrm f}(a)p$. No choice is involved: the
path is part of the data.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pointed homotopy]
$P\simeq_* Q$ iff there is a natural isomorphism $\alpha\colon P^{\mathrm f}\Rightarrow
Q^{\mathrm f}$ with $\alpha_c\,q=p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}
$\simeq_*$ is an equivalence relation; write $[(C,c),(D,d)]_*$ for the quotient set.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Invariance]\label{prop:invariance}
If $P\simeq_* Q$ then $P_\#=Q_\#$, an equality of homomorphisms.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
From $\alpha_c q=p$ we get $p^{-1}=q^{-1}\alpha_c^{-1}$, and naturality gives
$P^{\mathrm f}(a)\alpha_c=\alpha_c Q^{\mathrm f}(a)$. Hence
$P_\#(a)=q^{-1}\alpha_c^{-1}P^{\mathrm f}(a)\alpha_c q=q^{-1}Q^{\mathrm f}(a)q=Q_\#(a)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pointed classification]\label{thm:pointed}
Let $(C,c)$ be connected at $c$ and let $(D,d)$ be an \emph{arbitrary} pointed groupoid.
Then
\[
  \Phi\colon [(C,c),(D,d)]_*\longrightarrow \Hom\bigl(\Aut(c),\Aut(d)\bigr),
  \qquad [P]\longmapsto P_\#
\]
is a bijection, with inverse $\varphi\mapsto[(R_\varphi,\mathrm{id}_d)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Well definedness is Proposition~\ref{prop:invariance}. Surjectivity: the pointed realization
$(R_\varphi,\mathrm{id}_d)$ induces $\varphi$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:realize}. Injectivity:
if $P_\#=Q_\#$, set $h=pq^{-1}\colon P^{\mathrm f}(c)\to Q^{\mathrm f}(c)$; the hypothesis
$p^{-1}P^{\mathrm f}(a)p=q^{-1}Q^{\mathrm f}(a)q$ rearranges to
$P^{\mathrm f}(a)\,h=h\,Q^{\mathrm f}(a)$, which is~\eqref{eq:intertwine}. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:prescribed} there is $\eta$ with $\eta_c=h$, and then $\eta_c q=p$, so
$P\simeq_* Q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For a connected $1$-type $K(G,1)$ and any $1$-type $Y$ with $\pi_1(Y,y)=H$,
$[(K(G,1),\star),(Y,y)]_*\cong\Hom(G,H)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}
Connectedness of the \emph{source} cannot be dropped: a functor out of a disconnected
groupoid is determined componentwise, and its behaviour away from the component of $c$ is
invisible to $\Aut(c)$.
\end{remark}

\section{Strict functoriality, the endomorphism monoid, Whitehead}\label{sec:strict}

\begin{definition}
$\mathbf 1_{(C,c)}=(\mathrm{id}_C,\mathrm{id}_c)$, and for $P\colon(C,c)\to(D,d)$,
$Q\colon(D,d)\to(E,e)$,
\[
  P\ast Q=\bigl(P^{\mathrm f}\,;\,Q^{\mathrm f},\;Q^{\mathrm f}(p)\,q\bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Strict functoriality]\label{thm:strict}
$(\mathbf 1_{(C,c)})_\#=\mathrm{id}_{\Aut(c)}$ and $(P\ast Q)_\#=Q_\#\circ P_\#$, as
equalities of homomorphisms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $a\in\Aut(c)$,
\[
  (P\ast Q)_\#(a)=\bigl(Q^{\mathrm f}(p)q\bigr)^{-1}Q^{\mathrm f}\bigl(P^{\mathrm f}(a)\bigr)
  \bigl(Q^{\mathrm f}(p)q\bigr)
  =q^{-1}Q^{\mathrm f}\bigl(p^{-1}P^{\mathrm f}(a)p\bigr)q=Q_\#\bigl(P_\#(a)\bigr). \qedhere
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}
Composition respects pointed homotopy, hence descends to classes; under
Theorem~\ref{thm:pointed} it corresponds to composition of homomorphisms.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Endomorphism monoid]\label{thm:monoid}
For $C$ connected at $c$, the set $[(C,c),(C,c)]_*$ is a monoid under composition and
\[
  [(C,c),(C,c)]_*\;\cong\;\End\bigl(\Aut(c)\bigr)
\]
as monoids, via $[P]\mapsto P_\#$.
\end{theorem}

By contrast the unpointed monoid of self-map classes of $K(G,1)$ is the monoid of
\emph{conjugacy classes} of endomorphisms of $G$.

\begin{theorem}[Pointed Whitehead theorem]\label{thm:whitehead}
Let $C$ be connected at $c$ and $P$ a pointed self-map of $(C,c)$. The following are
equivalent: (i) $P^{\mathrm f}$ is an equivalence of groupoids; (ii) $P_\#$ is bijective;
(iii) $[P]$ is a unit of the monoid $[(C,c),(C,c)]_*$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$P_\#$ is $F_*$ followed by an isomorphism, so (ii) is bijectivity of
$F_*\colon\Aut(c)\to\Aut(P^{\mathrm f}(c))$. An equivalence induces bijections on vertex
groups; conversely a functor of connected groupoids bijective on one vertex group is
essentially surjective (connectedness) and fully faithful (each hom-set is a torsor over the
vertex group, identified with $\Aut(c)$ by the chosen arrows). (ii)$\Leftrightarrow$(iii) by
Theorem~\ref{thm:monoid}, since the units of $\End(G)$ are the bijective endomorphisms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:autG}
The group of pointed homotopy classes of pointed self-homotopy-equivalences of a connected
$1$-type with fundamental group $G$ is $\Aut(G)$, whereas the unpointed answer is
$\Out(G)=\Aut(G)/\Inn(G)$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Forgetting the basepoint: the exact fibres}\label{sec:fibres}

\begin{definition}
$\pi\colon[(C,c),(D,d)]_*\to[C,D]$, $[P]\mapsto[P^{\mathrm f}]$, where $[C,D]$ denotes
natural-isomorphism classes of functors.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Fibres are conjugation orbits]\label{prop:orbits}
For $C$ connected at $c$ and pointed maps $P,Q$,
\[
  \pi[P]=\pi[Q]\iff \exists\,u\in\Aut(d)\ \forall a\in\Aut(c):\;Q_\#(a)=u\,P_\#(a)\,u^{-1}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) A natural isomorphism $\alpha\colon P^{\mathrm f}\Rightarrow Q^{\mathrm f}$
gives $u=q^{-1}\alpha_c^{-1}p$, and naturality yields the conjugation identity.
($\Leftarrow$) By Theorem~\ref{thm:pointed} each map is homotopic to the realization of its
induced homomorphism, and $R_\varphi\cong R_\psi$ for conjugate $\varphi,\psi$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:prescribed} applied with $h=u$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
Under the two classifications, $\pi$ is the canonical surjection
$\Hom(G,H)\twoheadrightarrow\Hom(G,H)/H$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Fibre-counting theorem]\label{thm:fibre}
Let $C$ be connected at $c$ with $G=\Aut(c)$, let $H=\Aut(d)$, and let
$\varphi\colon G\to H$ be a homomorphism. Then
\[
  \bigl\lvert \pi^{-1}\bigl([R_\varphi]\bigr)\bigr\rvert
  \;=\;\bigl[\,H:C_H(\varphi(G))\,\bigr],
\]
the index of the centraliser of the image, uniformly in the basepoint and the models.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:pointed} and Proposition~\ref{prop:orbits} the fibre is the orbit of
$\varphi$ under the conjugation action of $H$ on $\Hom(G,H)$. Its stabiliser is
$\{u\in H: u\varphi(g)u^{-1}=\varphi(g)\ \forall g\}=C_H(\varphi(G))$, so orbit--stabiliser
gives the index.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Over the identity]\label{cor:identity}
With $C=D$, $c=d$ and $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_G$ we get
$\lvert\pi^{-1}([\mathrm{id}])\rvert=[G:Z(G)]=\lvert\Inn(G)\rvert$: the kernel size of
$\Aut(G)\twoheadrightarrow\Out(G)$, reconciling Corollary~\ref{cor:autG} with the unpointed
computation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Abelian target]\label{cor:abelian}
If $H$ is abelian then $\pi$ is injective: for a target with abelian fundamental group the
pointed and unpointed classifications coincide and basepoints carry no information.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}
Corollary~\ref{cor:abelian} explains why basepoint dependence is invisible in the first
examples one meets: maps into the circle are classified by $\Hom(\pi_1X,\mathbb Z)$ with no
conjugation quotient, and self-maps of the torus by integer matrices. Non-commutativity of
the target fundamental group is exactly the source of the phenomenon.
\end{remark}

\section{The decisive finite test: $G=H=S_3$}\label{sec:s3}

Let $S_3=\mathrm{Sym}\{0,1,2\}$, $\tau=(0\,1)$, and let $\sgn$ be the sign character. Work
with $K(S_3,1)=\BG S_3$.

\begin{lemma}
$\lvert\Hom(S_3,S_3)\rvert=10$: the trivial map; three maps with image of order two, of the
form $g\mapsto\tau$ if $\sgn(g)=-1$ and $g\mapsto1$ otherwise, composed with a choice of one
of the three transposition subgroups; and six automorphisms, all inner. There is no
homomorphism with image of order three, since no subgroup of order two of $S_3$ is normal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}
$Z(S_3)=\{1\}$, $C_{S_3}(\{1\})=S_3$ of order $6$, and $C_{S_3}(\{1,\tau\})=\{1,\tau\}$ of
order $2$.
\end{lemma}

Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:fibre}:

\begin{theorem}
The fibre of $\pi$ over the unpointed class of the constant self-map of $K(S_3,1)$ has
exactly $[S_3:C_{S_3}(\{1\})]=1$ element.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}
The fibre over the unpointed class of a map inducing a homomorphism with image of order two
has exactly $[S_3:C_{S_3}(\{1,\tau\})]=3$ elements.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}
The fibre over the unpointed class of the identity map of $K(S_3,1)$ has exactly
$[S_3:Z(S_3)]=6$ elements: the identity map admits six pairwise non-pointed-homotopic
pointed structures, corresponding to the six inner automorphisms of $S_3$, all homotopic
once the basepoint is forgotten.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
$K(S_3,1)$ has ten pointed self-map classes but only three unpointed ones; its pointed

self-equivalence group is $\Out(S_3)=1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[The abelian antipode]
Let $A$ be abelian and $(C,c)$ any connected pointed $1$-type. Then forgetting the basepoint
is injective on $[(C,c),(K(A,1),\star)]_*$; for $A=\mathbb Z/n$ the pointed and unpointed
classifications agree exactly. The contrast with the previous theorem --- six versus one ---
is the content of the theory in a single comparison.
\end{theorem}

\section{Algorithms and complexity}\label{sec:algo}

\paragraph{Enumerating $\Hom(G,H)$.} Choose generators $g_1,\dots,g_k$ of $G$ greedily. For
each tuple $(h_1,\dots,h_k)\in H^k$ attempt to extend $g_i\mapsto h_i$ by breadth-first
closure of the Cayley graph, assigning $xg_i\mapsto\varphi(x)h_i$ and aborting on conflict.
Cost $O(\lvert H\rvert^k\lvert G\rvert k)$ with $k\le\log_2\lvert G\rvert$.

\paragraph{Centralisers.} $C_H(S)$ is a scan costing $O(\lvert H\rvert\lvert S\rvert)$
multiplications; the index is $\lvert H\rvert/\lvert C_H(S)\rvert$.

\paragraph{Fibre count.} Compute $\im\varphi$, then $C_H(\im\varphi)$, then the index: cost
$O(\lvert G\rvert+\lvert H\rvert\lvert\im\varphi\rvert)$. This is far cheaper than
enumerating the orbit of $\varphi$ directly; Theorem~\ref{thm:fibre} converts an orbit
enumeration into a subgroup index.

\section{Applications}\label{sec:appl}

\paragraph{Covering spaces.} Pointed connected coverings of $(X,x)$ correspond to subgroups
of $\pi_1(X,x)$, unpointed ones to conjugacy classes of subgroups; the count of pointed
coverings over a given unpointed one is the index of a normaliser, the ``subobject'' analogue
of Theorem~\ref{thm:fibre}.

\paragraph{Group extensions.} Non-abelian extensions are governed by an outer action
$Q\to\Out(N)$, and lifting it to $Q\to\Aut(N)$ is obstructed. Corollary~\ref{cor:identity}
identifies the ambiguity of the lift with a fibre of size $[N:Z(N)]$.

\paragraph{Flat bundles and gauge theory.} A flat $H$-bundle on a space with fundamental
group $G$ is a holonomy $\varphi\colon G\to H$ up to $H$-conjugation; $C_H(\varphi(G))$ is the
unbroken symmetry group of the connection, and $[H:C_H(\varphi(G))]$ counts framings modulo
gauge equivalence.

\paragraph{Rigidity and computation.} Theorems~\ref{thm:monoid}--\ref{thm:whitehead} say that
the pointed homotopy theory of aspherical spaces is isomorphic, not merely equivalent, to the
algebra of their fundamental groups; deciding homotopy equivalence or counting homotopy
classes becomes finite group computation.

\section{Discussion and future directions}\label{sec:future}

With basepoints fixed, all comparison $2$-cells in the classification may be chosen to be
identities (Theorem~\ref{thm:strict}), so no coherence obstruction arises in the pointed
setting; what remains is the unpointed bicategorical bookkeeping, namely exhibiting
``connected pointed groupoid $\mapsto$ vertex group'' as a biequivalence onto the
$2$-category of groups, homomorphisms and conjugations.

For disconnected sources, a homotopy class of maps should be exactly the data, for each
source component, of a target component together with a (conjugacy class of a) homomorphism
of the corresponding fundamental groups; the pointed theory above supplies the componentwise
strict version.

One expects a characterisation of asphericity: a path-connected $X$ is aspherical iff for
every path-connected $Y$ the map $[Y,X]\to\Hom(\pi_1Y,\pi_1X)/\text{conj}$ is a bijection,
with the pointed analogue $[Y,X]_*\to\Hom(\pi_1Y,\pi_1X)$.

Finally, for a fixed finite $H$ the multiset
$\{[H:C_H(\varphi(G))]:\varphi\in\Hom(G,H)\}$ is an invariant of $(G,H)$ refining the count of
unpointed classes; it is $\{1,3,6\}$ for $G=H=S_3$ and
$\{1,3,3,3,6,6,6,6,6,6,6\}$ for $G=(\mathbb Z/2)^2$, $H=S_4$ (summing to $52$ homomorphisms
in $11$ orbits).

lists of elements with a multiplication table, and homomorphisms as dictionaries.

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Elem = Hashable
Hom = Tuple[Tuple[Elem, Elem], ...]  # a homomorphism, as a sorted tuple of pairs


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#  A minimal finite group class
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class FiniteGroup:
    """A finite group given by its element list and multiplication function."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, elements: Sequence[Elem],
                 mul: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem], one: Elem) -> None:
        self.name: str = name
        self.elements: List[Elem] = list(elements)
        self.mul: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem] = mul
        self.one: Elem = one

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.elements)

    def inv(self, g: Elem) -> Elem:
        for h in self.elements:
            if self.mul(g, h) == self.one:
                return h
        raise ValueError(f"no inverse for {g!r} in {self.name}")

    def conjugate(self, u: Elem, g: Elem) -> Elem:
        """Return u * g * u^{-1}."""
        return self.mul(self.mul(u, g), self.inv(u))

    def centralizer(self, subset: Sequence[Elem]) -> List[Elem]:
        """C_G(S) = { x : x s = s x for all s in S }."""
        return [x for x in self.elements
                if all(self.mul(x, s) == self.mul(s, x) for s in subset)]

    def centre(self) -> List[Elem]:
        return self.centralizer(self.elements)

    def generators(self) -> List[Elem]:
        """A small generating set found greedily (used to speed up hom search)."""
        gens: List[Elem] = []
        span = {self.one}
        for g in self.elements:
            if g in span:
                continue
            gens.append(g)
            span = self._closure(gens)
            if len(span) == self.order:
                break
        return gens

    def _closure(self, gens: Sequence[Elem]) -> set:
        span = {self.one}
        frontier = [self.one]
        while frontier:
            x = frontier.pop()
            for g in gens:
                y = self.mul(x, g)
                if y not in span:
                    span.add(y)
                    frontier.append(y)
        return span


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#  Concrete groups
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def cyclic(n: int) -> FiniteGroup:
    """The cyclic group Z/n, written additively but multiplied as a group."""
    return FiniteGroup(f"Z/{n}", list(range(n)), lambda a, b: (a + b) % n, 0)


def klein_four() -> FiniteGroup:
    """The Klein four group (Z/2)^2."""
    els = [(a, b) for a in (0, 1) for b in (0, 1)]
    return FiniteGroup("(Z/2)^2", els,
                       lambda x, y: ((x[0] + y[0]) % 2, (x[1] + y[1]) % 2), (0, 0))


def symmetric(n: int) -> FiniteGroup:
    """The symmetric group S_n, elements are tuples encoding permutations."""
    els = list(permutations_of(n))
    one = tuple(range(n))

    def mul(p: Elem, q: Elem) -> Elem:
        # (p*q)(i) = p(q(i))
        return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(n))  # type: ignore[index]

    return FiniteGroup(f"S_{n}", els, mul, one)


def permutations_of(n: int) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    if n == 0:
        return [()]
    out: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for smaller in permutations_of(n - 1):
        for pos in range(n):
            out.append(smaller[:pos] + (n - 1,) + smaller[pos:])
    return out


def dihedral(n: int) -> FiniteGroup:
    """The dihedral group of order 2n, elements (r, s) with r in Z/n, s in {0,1}."""
    els = [(r, s) for s in (0, 1) for r in range(n)]

    def mul(x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
        r1, s1 = x  # type: ignore[misc]
        r2, s2 = y  # type: ignore[misc]
        if s1 == 0:
            return ((r1 + r2) % n, s2)
        return ((r1 - r2) % n, (s1 + s2) % 2)

    return FiniteGroup(f"D_{n}", els, mul, (0, 0))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#  Homomorphisms, conjugation orbits, and the two classifications
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def all_homomorphisms(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup) -> List[Dict[Elem, Elem]]:
    """Enumerate Hom(G, H) by assigning images to a generating set of G."""
    gens = G.generators()
    homs: List[Dict[Elem, Elem]] = []
    for images in product(H.elements, repeat=len(gens)):
        phi = extend_to_hom(G, H, gens, images)
        if phi is not None:
            homs.append(phi)
    return homs


def extend_to_hom(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup, gens: Sequence[Elem],
                  images: Sequence[Elem]) -> Dict[Elem, Elem] | None:
    """Try to extend gens -> images to a homomorphism; return None if impossible."""
    phi: Dict[Elem, Elem] = {G.one: H.one}
    frontier = [G.one]
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for g, hg in zip(gens, images):
            y = G.mul(x, g)
            hy = H.mul(phi[x], hg)
            if y in phi:
                if phi[y] != hy:
                    return None
            else:
                phi[y] = hy
                frontier.append(y)
    if len(phi) != G.order:
        return None
    # final check of multiplicativity on all pairs
    for a in G.elements:
        for b in G.elements:
            if phi[G.mul(a, b)] != H.mul(phi[a], phi[b]):
                return None
    return phi


def freeze(phi: Dict[Elem, Elem], G: FiniteGroup) -> Hom:
    return tuple((g, phi[g]) for g in G.elements)


def conjugate_hom(H: FiniteGroup, u: Elem, phi: Dict[Elem, Elem]) -> Dict[Elem, Elem]:
    return {g: H.conjugate(u, h) for g, h in phi.items()}


def conjugation_orbits(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup) -> List[List[Hom]]:
    """Partition Hom(G,H) into orbits of the conjugation action of H."""
    homs = all_homomorphisms(G, H)
    seen: set = set()
    orbits: List[List[Hom]] = []
    for phi in homs:
        key = freeze(phi, G)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        orbit = set()
        for u in H.elements:
            orbit.add(freeze(conjugate_hom(H, u, phi), G))
        seen |= orbit
        orbits.append(sorted(orbit))
    return orbits


def centralizer_index_of_image(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup,
                               phi: Dict[Elem, Elem]) -> int:
    """[H : C_H(phi(G))]."""
    image = sorted(set(phi.values()), key=repr)
    return H.order // len(H.centralizer(image))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#  Automorphisms, inner automorphisms, and Out
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def automorphisms(G: FiniteGroup) -> List[Dict[Elem, Elem]]:
    return [phi for phi in all_homomorphisms(G, G)
            if len(set(phi.values())) == G.order]


def inner_automorphisms(G: FiniteGroup) -> List[Hom]:
    return sorted({freeze({g: G.conjugate(u, g) for g in G.elements}, G)
                   for u in G.elements})


def out_order(G: FiniteGroup) -> int:
    return len(automorphisms(G)) // len(inner_automorphisms(G))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#  The demonstrations
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def demo_fibre_theorem(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup) -> None:
    """Check: every conjugation orbit has size [H : C_H(image)]."""
    print(f"\n--- Fibres of  [K({G.name},1), K({H.name},1)]_*  ->  "
          f"[K({G.name},1), K({H.name},1)] ---")
    orbits = conjugation_orbits(G, H)
    total = sum(len(o) for o in orbits)
    print(f"|Hom({G.name},{H.name})| = {total}   "
          f"(= number of POINTED homotopy classes)")
    print(f"number of conjugation orbits = {len(orbits)}   "
          f"(= number of UNPOINTED homotopy classes)")
    print(f"{'orbit size':>12} {'[H:C_H(im)]':>13} {'|image|':>8}  agree?")
    for orbit in sorted(orbits, key=len):
        rep = dict(orbit[0])
        predicted = centralizer_index_of_image(G, H, rep)
        image_size = len(set(rep.values()))
        ok = "yes" if predicted == len(orbit) else "NO!"
        print(f"{len(orbit):>12} {predicted:>13} {image_size:>8}  {ok}")
        assert predicted == len(orbit), "fibre theorem violated"


def demo_s3_test() -> None:
    """The decisive finite test: G = H = S_3, fibre sizes 1, 3, 6."""
    S3 = symmetric(3)
    print("\n=== The S_3 test =======================================")
    orbits = sorted(conjugation_orbits(S3, S3), key=len)
    sizes = [len(o) for o in orbits]
    print(f"orbit sizes of the conjugation action of S_3 on Hom(S_3,S_3): {sizes}")
    assert sizes == [1, 3, 6], sizes
    assert sum(sizes) == 10
    print("Interpretation:")
    print("  * over the class of the CONSTANT map          : 1 pointed class")
    print("  * over the class of the sign-and-swap map     : 3 pointed classes")
    print("  * over the class of the IDENTITY map          : 6 pointed classes")
    print("So the identity map of K(S_3,1) has six pairwise non-pointed-homotopic")
    print("pointed representatives, all homotopic once basepoints are forgotten.")
    centre = S3.centre()
    print(f"  [S_3 : Z(S_3)] = {S3.order // len(centre)} = 6, "
          f"and |Z(S_3)| = {len(centre)}")


def demo_abelian_case() -> None:
    """For abelian target, forgetting the basepoint is injective."""
    print("\n=== The abelian extreme ================================")
    for H in [cyclic(2), cyclic(6), klein_four(), cyclic(12)]:
        for G in [cyclic(4), symmetric(3), dihedral(4)]:
            orbits = conjugation_orbits(G, H)
            total = sum(len(o) for o in orbits)
            assert all(len(o) == 1 for o in orbits)
            print(f"  Hom({G.name:>4}, {H.name:>7}): "
                  f"{total:>3} pointed classes = {len(orbits):>3} unpointed "
                  f"classes  (all fibres of size 1)")


def demo_self_equivalences() -> None:
    """Pointed self-equivalences = Aut G;  unpointed = Out G."""
    print("\n=== Self-equivalences of K(G,1):  Aut G  versus  Out G ==")
    print(f"{'G':>8} {'|G|':>4} {'|Aut G|':>8} {'|Inn G|':>8} "
          f"{'|Out G|':>8} {'[G:Z(G)]':>9}")
    for G in [cyclic(1), cyclic(2), cyclic(4), cyclic(6), klein_four(),
              symmetric(3), dihedral(4), cyclic(8), symmetric(4)]:
        aut = len(automorphisms(G))
        inn = len(inner_automorphisms(G))
        idx = G.order // len(G.centre())
        assert inn == idx, "Inn G is not G/Z(G)"
        print(f"{G.name:>8} {G.order:>4} {aut:>8} {inn:>8} "
              f"{aut // inn:>8} {idx:>9}")
    print("The fibre of  Aut G  ->  Out G  over the identity class has "
          "[G:Z(G)] elements,")
    print("exactly the general fibre count applied to phi = id.")


def demo_strict_functoriality() -> None:
    """Composition of pointed classes is composition of homomorphisms, on the nose."""
    print("\n=== Strict functoriality of the pointed classification ==")
    S3 = symmetric(3)
    homs = all_homomorphisms(S3, S3)
    bad = 0
    for phi in homs:
        for psi in homs:
            comp = {g: psi[phi[g]] for g in S3.elements}
            # composition of pointed classes = composition of homomorphisms
            if any(comp[S3.mul(a, b)] != S3.mul(comp[a], comp[b])
                   for a in S3.elements for b in S3.elements):
                bad += 1
    print(f"checked {len(homs)**2} composites of pointed classes; "
          f"failures: {bad}")
    assert bad == 0
    print("By contrast, unpointed composition is only well defined on")
    print("conjugacy classes: the induced homomorphism of a composite is")
    print("merely CONJUGATE to the composite of the induced homomorphisms.")
    # exhibit the unpointed ambiguity concretely
    orbits = conjugation_orbits(S3, S3)
    reps = [dict(o[0]) for o in orbits]
    print("Composition table of the three unpointed classes "
          "(monoid of conjugacy classes of endomorphisms):")
    labels = {freeze(r, S3): i for i, o in enumerate(orbits) for r in [dict(x) for x in o]}
    for i, a in enumerate(reps):
        row = []
        for j, b in enumerate(reps):
            comp = {g: b[a[g]] for g in S3.elements}
            row.append(labels[freeze(comp, S3)])
        print(f"   class {i} composed with each class -> {row}")


def main() -> None:
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Pointed and unpointed classification of maps of 1-types")
    print("=" * 60)
    demo_s3_test()
    demo_fibre_theorem(symmetric(3), symmetric(3))
    demo_fibre_theorem(cyclic(6), symmetric(3))
    demo_fibre_theorem(symmetric(3), dihedral(4))
    demo_fibre_theorem(klein_four(), symmetric(4))
    demo_abelian_case()
    demo_self_equivalences()
    demo_strict_functoriality()
    print("\nAll assertions passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        orbit = set()
        for u in H.elements:
            orbit.add(freeze(conjugate_hom(H, u, phi), G))
        seen |= orbit
        orbits.append(sorted(orbit))
    return orbits


def centralizer_index_of_image(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup,
                               phi: Dict[Elem, Elem]) -> int:
    """[H : C_H(phi(G))]."""
    image = sorted(set(phi.values()), key=repr)
    return H.order // len(H.centralizer(image))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#  Automorphisms, inner automorphisms, and Out
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def automorphisms(G: FiniteGroup) -> List[Dict[Elem, Elem]]:
    return [phi for phi in all_homomorphisms(G, G)
            if len(set(phi.values())) == G.order]


def inner_automorphisms(G: FiniteGroup) -> List[Hom]:
    return sorted({freeze({g: G.conjugate(u, g) for g in G.elements}, G)
                   for u in G.elements})


def out_order(G: FiniteGroup) -> int:
    return len(automorphisms(G)) // len(inner_automorphisms(G))

def demo_fibre_theorem(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup) -> None:
    """Check: every conjugation orbit has size [H : C_H(image)]."""
    print(f"\n--- Fibres of  [K({G.name},1), K({H.name},1)]_*  ->  "
          f"[K({G.name},1), K({H.name},1)] ---")
    orbits = conjugation_orbits(G, H)
    total = sum(len(o) for o in orbits)
    print(f"|Hom({G.name},{H.name})| = {total}   "
          f"(= number of POINTED homotopy classes)")
    print(f"number of conjugation orbits = {len(orbits)}   "
          f"(= number of UNPOINTED homotopy classes)")
    print(f"{'orbit size':>12} {'[H:C_H(im)]':>13} {'|image|':>8}  agree?")
    for orbit in sorted(orbits, key=len):
        rep = dict(orbit[0])
        predicted = centralizer_index_of_image(G, H, rep)
        image_size = len(set(rep.values()))
        ok = "yes" if predicted == len(orbit) else "NO!"
        print(f"{len(orbit):>12} {predicted:>13} {image_size:>8}  {ok}")
        assert predicted == len(orbit), "fibre theorem violated"

    S3 = symmetric(3)

    sizes = [len(o) for o in orbits]
    print(f"orbit sizes of the conjugation action of S_3 on Hom(S_3,S_3): {sizes}")

    print("  * over the class of the sign-and-swap map     : 3 pointed classes")
    print("  * over the class of the IDENTITY map          : 6 pointed classes")

    print("pointed representatives, all homotopic once basepoints are forgotten.")

    """Composition of pointed classes is composition of homomorphisms, on the nose."""
    print("\n=== Strict functoriality of the pointed classification ==")
    S3 = symmetric(3)
    homs = all_homomorphisms(S3, S3)
    bad = 0
    for phi in homs:

            comp = {g: psi[phi[g]] for g in S3.elements}

            if any(comp[S3.mul(a, b)] != S3.mul(comp[a], comp[b])

          f"failures: {bad}")

    print("conjugacy classes: the induced homomorphism of a composite is")

            row.append(labels[freeze(comp, S3)])

def mul(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    """(p*q)(i) = p(q(i))."""
    return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(3))

    g1, g2 = (1, 0, 2), (1, 2, 0)

    for h1, h2 in product(S3, repeat=2):
        phi: Dict[Perm, Perm] = {ONE: ONE}
        frontier = [ONE]
        ok = True
        while frontier and ok:
            x = frontier.pop()
            for g, h in ((g1, h1), (g2, h2)):
                y, hy = mul(x, g), mul(phi[x], h)
                if y in phi:

                else:

    return {g: psi[phi[g]] for g in S3}

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, List, Optional, Sequence

Elem = Hashable


class FiniteGroup:
    """A finite group given by an element list, a product, and a unit."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, elements: Sequence[Elem],
                 mul: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem], one: Elem) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.elements: List[Elem] = list(elements)
        self.mul = mul
        self.one = one

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.elements)

    def closure(self, gens: Sequence[Elem]) -> set:
        span = {self.one}
        frontier = [self.one]
        while frontier:
            x = frontier.pop()
            for g in gens:
                y = self.mul(x, g)
                if y not in span:
                    span.add(y)
                    frontier.append(y)
        return span

    def generators(self) -> List[Elem]:
        """A small generating set, found greedily."""
        gens: List[Elem] = []
        span = {self.one}
        for g in self.elements:
            if g in span:
                continue
            gens.append(g)
            span = self.closure(gens)
            if len(span) == self.order:
                break
        return gens


def lift_generators(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup, gens: Sequence[Elem],
                    images: Sequence[Elem]) -> Optional[Dict[Elem, Elem]]:
    """Extend the assignment gens[i] |-> images[i] to a homomorphism, or fail.

    Breadth-first closure of the Cayley graph of G with respect to `gens`:
    whenever x has an image, x*g_i must receive the image phi(x)*h_i.  A clash
    means the assignment does not respect the relations of G, so no homomorphism
    extends it.
    """
    phi: Dict[Elem, Elem] = {G.one: H.one}
    frontier: List[Elem] = [G.one]
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for g, h in zip(gens, images):
            y = G.mul(x, g)
            hy = H.mul(phi[x], h)
            if y in phi:
                if phi[y] != hy:
                    return None
            else:
                phi[y] = hy
                frontier.append(y)
    return phi if len(phi) == G.order else None


def all_homomorphisms(G: FiniteGroup, H: FiniteGroup) -> List[Dict[Elem, Elem]]:
    """Enumerate Hom(G, H).  Cost O(|H|^k * |G| * k) with k = #generators."""
    gens = G.generators()
    homs: List[Dict[Elem, Elem]] = []
    for images in product(H.elements, repeat=len(gens)):
        phi = lift_generators(G, H, gens, images)
        if phi is not None:
            homs.append(phi)
    return homs

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence

Elem = Hashable


def centralizer(elements: Sequence[Elem], mul: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem],
                subset: Sequence[Elem]) -> List[Elem]:
    """C_H(S) = { x in H : x s = s x for every s in S }."""
    return [x for x in elements if all(mul(x, s) == mul(s, x) for s in subset)]


def fibre_size(order_H: int, elements_H: Sequence[Elem],
               mul_H: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem],
               phi_values: Sequence[Elem]) -> int:
    """Number of pointed homotopy classes over one unpointed class.

    Given the list of values phi(g), g in G, of the homomorphism induced by the
    map, the fibre of  [X,Y]_* -> [X,Y]  over its unpointed class has exactly
    [H : C_H(phi(G))] elements.  Complexity: O(|H| * |image|) multiplications,
    versus O(|H| * |G|) for a direct orbit enumeration.
    """
    image = list(dict.fromkeys(phi_values))            # de-duplicate, keep order
    cent = centralizer(elements_H, mul_H, image)       # stabiliser of phi
    assert order_H % len(cent) == 0, "Lagrange violated: bad group data"
    return order_H // len(cent)


def fibre_profile(order_H: int, elements_H: Sequence[Elem],
                  mul_H: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem],
                  homs: Sequence[Dict[Elem, Elem]]) -> List[int]:
    """The multiset of fibre sizes over all unpointed classes, sorted.

    The sizes returned sum to |Hom(G,H)| = number of POINTED classes, and their
    count is the number of UNPOINTED classes.
    """
    seen: List[frozenset] = []
    sizes: List[int] = []
    for phi in homs:
        image = frozenset(phi.values())
        # two homomorphisms in the same orbit have conjugate, hence equal-size,
        # images; we still test orbit membership exactly, by conjugating phi.
        key = frozenset(
            frozenset(_conj(mul_H, elements_H, u, phi).items()) for u in elements_H
        )
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.append(key)
        sizes.append(fibre_size(order_H, elements_H, mul_H, list(image)))
    return sorted(sizes)


def _conj(mul_H: Callable[[Elem, Elem], Elem], elements_H: Sequence[Elem],
          u: Elem, phi: Dict[Elem, Elem]) -> Dict[Elem, Elem]:
    """u . phi : g |-> u phi(g) u^{-1}."""
    one = next(e for e in elements_H
               if all(mul_H(e, x) == x for x in elements_H))
    uinv = next(v for v in elements_H if mul_H(u, v) == one)
    return {g: mul_H(mul_H(u, h), uinv) for g, h in phi.items()}

        if ok and len(phi) == 6 and \
                all(phi[mul(a, b)] == mul(phi[a], phi[b]) for a in S3 for b in S3):
            out.append(phi)
    return out


def orbits() -> List[List[Dict[Perm, Perm]]]:
    ends = endomorphisms()
    seen: set = set()
    out: List[List[Dict[Perm, Perm]]] = []
    for phi in ends:
        k = tuple(phi[g] for g in S3)
        if k in seen:
            continue
        orb: Dict[Tuple[Perm, ...], Dict[Perm, Perm]] = {}
        for u in S3:
            ui = inv(u)
            psi = {g: mul(mul(u, h), ui) for g, h in phi.items()}
            orb[tuple(psi[g] for g in S3)] = psi
        seen |= set(orb)
        out.append(list(orb.values()))
    return sorted(out, key=len)

    image = set(phi.values())
    cent = [x for x in S3 if all(mul(x, s) == mul(s, x) for s in image)]
    return 6 // len(cent)

<details>
<summary>Why the fibre size is a centraliser index (click to reveal the argument)</summary>
<p>
A pointed map $(X,x) \to (Y,y)$ is a map $F$ <em>together with</em> a chosen path from
$F(x)$ to $y$; it induces a homomorphism
$\varphi = F_\# : \pi_1(X,x) \to \pi_1(Y,y)$ with no choices at all. Two pointed maps are
pointed homotopic exactly when they induce the <em>same</em> homomorphism, so pointed
classes $=$ $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$.
</p>
<p>
Changing the chosen path replaces $\varphi$ by $u\varphi(\cdot)u^{-1}$ for some
$u \in H$, and every such $u$ occurs, so two pointed classes become equal after forgetting
the basepoint exactly when the homomorphisms are conjugate. Therefore the fibres of the
forgetful map are the orbits of the conjugation action of $H$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$.
</p>
<p>
The stabiliser of $\varphi$ under that action is
$\{u : u\varphi(g)u^{-1} = \varphi(g) \text{ for all } g\}$, which is precisely the
centraliser $C_H(\varphi(G))$ of the image. The orbit–stabiliser theorem then gives
$$ |\text{fibre over } [\varphi]| \;=\; [\,H : C_H(\varphi(G))\,]. $$
Taking $G = H$ and $\varphi = \mathrm{id}$, the image is everything and its centraliser is
the centre, so the identity map of $K(G,1)$ has $[G : Z(G)] = |\mathrm{Inn}(G)|$ pointed
refinements — the reason the pointed self-equivalence group is $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$
while the unpointed one is $\mathrm{Out}(G)$.
</p>
</details>

<li><b>$G$ cyclic.</b> Homomorphisms out of $\mathbb{Z}/n$ are elements of order dividing

</ul>

<script>
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- groups ----
function cyclic(n) {
  const els = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) els.push(String(i));
  return { name: "Z/" + n, els: els, one: "0",
           mul: (a, b) => String((parseInt(a) + parseInt(b)) % n) };
}
function product2(n, m) {
  const els = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) for (let j = 0; j < m; j++) els.push(i + "," + j);
  return { name: "Z/" + n + " x Z/" + m, els: els, one: "0,0",
    mul: (a, b) => {
      const p = a.split(","), q = b.split(",");
      return ((+p[0] + +q[0]) % n) + "," + ((+p[1] + +q[1]) % m);
    } };
}
function symmetric(n) {
  const perms = [];
  (function rec(cur, rest) {
    if (rest.length === 0) { perms.push(cur.slice()); return; }
    for (let i = 0; i < rest.length; i++) {
      const r = rest.slice(); const x = r.splice(i, 1)[0];
      rec(cur.concat([x]), r);
    }
  })([], Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => i));
  const els = perms.map(p => p.join(""));
  const idn = Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => i).join("");
  return { name: "S_" + n, els: els, one: idn,
    mul: (a, b) => {
      let out = "";
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out += a[+b[i]];
      return out;
    } };
}
function dihedral(n) {
  const els = [];
  for (let s = 0; s < 2; s++) for (let r = 0; r < n; r++) els.push(r + "|" + s);
  return { name: "D_" + n + " (order " + (2 * n) + ")", els: els, one: "0|0",
    mul: (a, b) => {
      const p = a.split("|"), q = b.split("|");
      const r1 = +p[0], s1 = +p[1], r2 = +q[0], s2 = +q[1];
      if (s1 === 0) return ((r1 + r2) % n) + "|" + s2;
      return (((r1 - r2) % n + n) % n) + "|" + ((s1 + s2) % 2);
    } };
}
function quaternion() {
  // Q8 = {1,-1,i,-i,j,-j,k,-k} by explicit table
  const els = ["1", "-1", "i", "-i", "j", "-j", "k", "-k"];
  const sgn = x => x[0] === "-" ? -1 : 1;
  const base = x => x.replace("-", "");
  const tbl = { "11": "1", "1i": "i", "1j": "j", "1k": "k",
                "i1": "i", "ii": "-1", "ij": "k", "ik": "-j",
                "j1": "j", "ji": "-k", "jj": "-1", "jk": "i",
                "k1": "k", "ki": "j", "kj": "-i", "kk": "-1" };
  return { name: "Q_8", els: els, one: "1",
    mul: (a, b) => {
      const s = sgn(a) * sgn(b);
      let r = tbl[base(a) + base(b)];
      const rs = sgn(r) * s;
      const rb = base(r);
      return rs < 0 ? "-" + rb : rb;
    } };
}

const GROUPS = [cyclic(1), cyclic(2), cyclic(3), cyclic(4), cyclic(6), cyclic(8),
                product2(2, 2), product2(2, 4), symmetric(3), dihedral(4),
                quaternion(), symmetric(4)];

// --------------------------------------------------- group computations ----
function inverse(G, g) {
  for (const h of G.els) if (G.mul(g, h) === G.one) return h;
  throw new Error("no inverse");
}
function closure(G, gens) {
  const span = new Set([G.one]); const stack = [G.one];
  while (stack.length) {
    const x = stack.pop();
    for (const g of gens) {
      const y = G.mul(x, g);
      if (!span.has(y)) { span.add(y); stack.push(y); }
    }
  }
  return span;
}
function generators(G) {
  const gens = []; let span = new Set([G.one]);
  for (const g of G.els) {
    if (span.has(g)) continue;
    gens.push(g); span = closure(G, gens);
    if (span.size === G.els.length) break;
  }
  return gens;
}
function liftGenerators(G, H, gens, images) {
  const phi = new Map([[G.one, H.one]]);
  const stack = [G.one];
  while (stack.length) {
    const x = stack.pop();
    for (let i = 0; i < gens.length; i++) {
      const y = G.mul(x, gens[i]);
      const hy = H.mul(phi.get(x), images[i]);
      if (phi.has(y)) { if (phi.get(y) !== hy) return null; }
      else { phi.set(y, hy); stack.push(y); }
    }
  }
  return phi.size === G.els.length ? phi : null;
}
function allHoms(G, H) {
  const gens = generators(G);
  const homs = [];
  const total = Math.pow(H.els.length, gens.length);
  for (let code = 0; code < total; code++) {
    const images = []; let c = code;
    for (let i = 0; i < gens.length; i++) {
      images.push(H.els[c % H.els.length]);
      c = Math.floor(c / H.els.length);
    }
    const phi = liftGenerators(G, H, gens, images);
    if (phi) homs.push(phi);
  }
  return homs;
}
function homKey(G, phi) { return G.els.map(g => phi.get(g)).join(";"); }
function conjugateHom(G, H, u, phi) {
  const ui = inverse(H, u);
  const out = new Map();
  for (const g of G.els) out.set(g, H.mul(H.mul(u, phi.get(g)), ui));
  return out;
}
function centralizer(H, subset) {
  return H.els.filter(x => subset.every(s => H.mul(x, s) === H.mul(s, x)));
}
function analyse(G, H) {
  const homs = allHoms(G, H);
  const seen = new Set(); const orbits = [];
  for (const phi of homs) {
    const k = homKey(G, phi);
    if (seen.has(k)) continue;
    const orb = new Map();
    for (const u of H.els) {
      const psi = conjugateHom(G, H, u, phi);
      orb.set(homKey(G, psi), psi);
    }
    for (const kk of orb.keys()) seen.add(kk);
    const image = Array.from(new Set(G.els.map(g => phi.get(g))));
    const cent = centralizer(H, image);
    orbits.push({ rep: phi, size: orb.size, image: image,
                  centSize: cent.length,
                  index: H.els.length / cent.length });
  }
  orbits.sort((a, b) => a.size - b.size);
  return { homs: homs, orbits: orbits };
}
function describe(G, H, phi) {
  const image = Array.from(new Set(G.els.map(g => phi.get(g))));
  if (image.length === 1) return "constant map";
  if (G === H && G.els.every(g => phi.get(g) === g)) return "identity";
  if (image.length === G.els.length) return "an automorphism onto its image";
  return "image of order " + image.length;
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------- drawing ----
const PALETTE = ["#2b6cb0", "#c05621", "#2f855a", "#6b46c1", "#b83280",
                 "#2c7a7b", "#975a16", "#4a5568"];

function draw(G, H, data) {
  const svg = document.getElementById("diagram");
  const W = 900, TOP = 70, BOT = 235;
  const orbits = data.orbits;
  const N = data.homs.length;
  const maxDots = 90;
  let parts = [];
  parts.push('<text x="8" y="30" font-size="13" fill="#5d6b7a">pointed classes '
    + '— ' + N + ' homomorphisms</text>');
  parts.push('<text x="8" y="285" font-size="13" fill="#5d6b7a">unpointed classes '
    + '— ' + orbits.length + ' conjugacy classes</text>');
  if (N > maxDots) {
    parts.push('<text x="450" y="160" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" '
      + 'fill="#c05621">' + N + ' pointed classes over ' + orbits.length
      + ' unpointed ones — too many to draw; see the table below.</text>');
    svg.innerHTML = parts.join("");
    return;
  }
  const slots = orbits.length;
  const colWidth = (W - 80) / slots;
  orbits.forEach((orb, i) => {
    const cx = 40 + colWidth * (i + 0.5);
    const col = PALETTE[i % PALETTE.length];
    const n = orb.size;
    const spread = Math.min(colWidth - 26, 24 * n);
    for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      const x = n === 1 ? cx : cx - spread / 2 + spread * j / (n - 1);
      parts.push('<line x1="' + x + '" y1="' + TOP + '" x2="' + cx + '" y2="'
        + BOT + '" stroke="' + col + '" stroke-width="1.3" opacity="0.65"/>');
      parts.push('<circle cx="' + x + '" cy="' + TOP + '" r="7" fill="' + col + '"/>');
    }
    parts.push('<rect x="' + (cx - 11) + '" y="' + (BOT - 11) + '" width="22" '
      + 'height="22" rx="4" fill="' + col + '"/>');
    parts.push('<text x="' + cx + '" y="' + (TOP - 30) + '" font-size="13" '
      + 'text-anchor="middle" fill="' + col + '">' + n + ' pointed</text>');
    parts.push('<text x="' + cx + '" y="' + (TOP - 14) + '" font-size="12" '
      + 'text-anchor="middle" fill="' + col + '">index ' + orb.index + '</text>');
    parts.push('<text x="' + cx + '" y="' + (BOT + 30) + '" font-size="12" '
      + 'text-anchor="middle" fill="#1b2430">' + describe(G, H, orb.rep)
      + '</text>');
  });
  svg.innerHTML = parts.join("");
}

function render() {
  const G = GROUPS[+document.getElementById("src").value];
  const H = GROUPS[+document.getElementById("tgt").value];
  const data = analyse(G, H);
  const N = data.homs.length, M = data.orbits.length;

  document.getElementById("stats").innerHTML =
    stat(N, "pointed homotopy classes = |Hom(G,H)|") +
    stat(M, "unpointed homotopy classes") +
    stat(H.els.length, "order of the target group H") +
    stat((N / M).toFixed(2), "average fibre size");

  document.getElementById("hint").innerHTML =
    "|G| = " + G.els.length + ", |H| = " + H.els.length +
    (isAbelian(H) ? " — H is abelian" : " — H is non-abelian");

  draw(G, H, data);

  const body = document.querySelector("#tbl tbody");
  body.innerHTML = data.orbits.map(function (o, i) {
    return "<tr><td>#" + (i + 1) + "</td><td>" + describe(G, H, o.rep)
      + "</td><td>" + o.image.length + "</td><td>" + o.centSize
      + "</td><td><b>" + o.index + "</b>" +
      (o.index === o.size ? "" : " ⚠") + "</td></tr>";
  }).join("");

  const ok = data.orbits.every(o => o.index === o.size);
  const v = document.getElementById("verdict");
  if (isAbelian(H)) {
    v.className = "verdict";
    v.innerHTML = "<b>Abelian target.</b> Conjugation is trivial, so every fibre "
      + "has one element: the pointed and unpointed classifications coincide and the "
      + "basepoint carries no information.";
  } else if (N === M) {
    v.className = "verdict";
    v.innerHTML = "<b>All fibres trivial here.</b> Every homomorphism has image inside "

  "interactive_layout": "# Where You Started Matters: A Guided Tour of Pointed Homotopy Classes

*A notebook-style walk through the classification of maps between spaces whose only
homotopy information is a fundamental group — and the exact price of forgetting a
basepoint.*

---

## 1. The question in one sentence

If two spaces are "nothing but their loops", a map between them ought to be "nothing but a
homomorphism of fundamental groups". Is it?

Almost. The classical answer is
$$[X, Y] \;\cong\; \operatorname{Hom}(G, H)\,/\,\text{conjugation by } H,$$
for $X$ and $Y$ aspherical with fundamental groups $G$ and $H$. The quotient is the ghost
in the machine. This page is about where it comes from, how to get rid of it, and exactly
how big it is.

Before any formalism, play with the phenomenon.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Set both groups to $S_3$ and look at the numbers: **ten** pointed classes collapse into
**three** unpointed ones, in bundles of sizes $1$, $3$ and $6$. Now set the target to any
cyclic group and watch the picture become a perfect matching. That contrast — non-abelian
target versus abelian target — is the entire story in miniature.

---

## 2. Spaces that are nothing but their loops

<details>
<summary><b>Background: what is a $K(G,1)$?</b> (click to expand)</summary>

A path-connected space $X$ is called *aspherical*, or a *homotopy $1$-type*, or a
[$K(G,1)$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilenberg%E2%80%93MacLane_space), if its
fundamental group is $G$ and it has no higher homotopy: no sphere of dimension $\ge 2$ can
detect anything in it. Examples:

* the circle $S^1$, with $\pi_1 = \mathbb{Z}$;
* the figure-eight, with $\pi_1$ the free group on two generators;
* any closed surface of genus $\ge 1$;
* the torus $T^n$, with $\pi_1 = \mathbb{Z}^n$;
* for *every* group $G$ whatsoever, a space $K(G,1)$ exists and is unique up to homotopy
  equivalence.

Because such a space carries no information beyond $G$, everything about it should be
expressible in group theory. Making "should be" into "is" is the business of this page.
</details>

The convenient algebraic model of a $1$-type is a **groupoid**: a collection of objects
with invertible arrows between them. Think of objects as points and arrows as homotopy
classes of paths. Then:

| topology | algebra |
|---|---|
| point of $X$ | object $c$ |
| $\pi_1(X, x)$ | the group $\operatorname{Aut}(c)$ of arrows $c \to c$ |
| path-connected | every two objects joined by an arrow |
| map $X \to Y$ | functor |
| homotopy | natural isomorphism |
| $K(G,1)$ | the groupoid with one object $\star$ and $\operatorname{Aut}(\star) = G$ |

From now on, "the model of $K(G,1)$" means that one-object groupoid: its arrows *are* the
elements of $G$, composed by multiplication.

---

## 3. Why conjugation appears at all

Here is the source of the ghost, and it is worth seeing rather than reading about. Take a
map, then take hold of the basepoint and drag it once around a loop $u$. When you let go,
the map is homotopic to what it was — you have just performed a homotopy — but the
homomorphism it induces has been replaced by
$$g \;\longmapsto\; u\,\varphi(g)\,u^{-1}.$$

{{interactive_demo:1}}

Try the identity map first and drag around each of the six loops of $S_3$: every drag gives
a genuinely different homomorphism, and you traverse an orbit of size $6$. Then try the
constant map: no drag changes anything, and the orbit has size $1$. Finally try one of the
sign maps: exactly two loops leave it alone — precisely the centraliser $\{1,\tau\}$ of its
image — and the orbit has size $3$.

You have just discovered the main theorem by hand.

---

## 4. The pointed classification

The fix is to make the basepoint part of the data.

> **Definition.** A **pointed map** $(X,x) \to (Y,y)$ is a map $F$ *together with* a chosen
> path from $F(x)$ to $y$. A **pointed homotopy** is a homotopy that is compatible with the
> chosen paths: sliding along the homotopy at the basepoint and then along the second chosen
> path must give the first chosen path.

With the path supplied as data, the induced homomorphism involves no choice at all:
$$F_\#(a) \;=\; p^{-1}\,F(a)\,p .$$

> **Pointed Classification Theorem.** For a **connected** pointed $1$-type $(X,x)$ with
> $\pi_1(X,x) = G$ and an **arbitrary** pointed $1$-type $(Y,y)$ with $\pi_1(Y,y) = H$,
> $$[(X,x),(Y,y)]_* \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \operatorname{Hom}(G,H), \qquad [F] \mapsto F_\# .$$
> No quotient. No conjugation. No connectedness assumption on the target.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof, and the lemma that powers it</b></summary>

**Surjectivity** is a construction. Given $\varphi : G \to H$, choose once and for all a
path $\gamma_P$ from the basepoint $x$ to each point $P$, and define a map sending every
point to $y$ and every arrow $f : P \to Q$ to $\varphi(\gamma_P f \gamma_Q^{-1})$ — close
$f$ up into a loop through the basepoint, then apply $\varphi$. Because closing up is
multiplicative, this is a map, and it induces $\varphi$.

**Injectivity** is the heart of the matter, and rests on:

> **Prescribed-Homotopy Lemma.** Let $X$ be connected at $x$, let $F, G$ be maps out of $X$,
> and let $h : F(x) \to G(x)$ be *any* path in the target satisfying the intertwining
> condition $F(a)\,h = h\,G(a)$ for every loop $a$ at $x$. Then there is a homotopy from $F$
> to $G$ whose value at the basepoint is exactly $h$.

*Proof.* Define the homotopy at the point $P$ to be
$$\eta_P \;=\; F(\gamma_P)^{-1}\, h\, G(\gamma_P):$$
travel back to the basepoint in the $F$-picture, cross over by $h$, travel out again in the
$G$-picture. For an arbitrary arrow $f : P \to Q$, the naturality square
$F(f)\,\eta_Q = \eta_P\,G(f)$ is exactly the intertwining condition applied to the loop
$\gamma_P f \gamma_Q^{-1}$. Since $\gamma_x$ is trivial, $\eta_x = h$. $\blacksquare$

Now suppose two pointed maps $(F,p)$ and $(G,q)$ induce the same homomorphism, i.e.
$p^{-1}F(a)p = q^{-1}G(a)q$ for all $a$. Rearranged, this says exactly that $h = pq^{-1}$
intertwines. The lemma gives a homotopy with value $h$ at the basepoint, and then
$\eta_x q = p$ — which is precisely the compatibility required of a *pointed* homotopy. So
the two pointed maps are pointed homotopic. $\blacksquare$

What earlier arguments give is *some* homotopy; what makes the pointed theory exact is
control over its value at the basepoint.
</details>

Two immediate dividends:

* **Strict functoriality.** The identity induces the identity, and a composite induces
  exactly the composite: $(F \ast G)_\# = G_\# \circ F_\#$, an equality rather than a
  conjugacy. Unpointed, the best one can say is "conjugate to".
* **$\operatorname{Aut}$, not $\operatorname{Out}$.** Pointed self-map classes of $K(G,1)$
  form a monoid isomorphic to $\operatorname{End}(G)$; a class is invertible exactly when it
  is a homotopy equivalence (the pointed Whitehead theorem), so the pointed
  self-equivalence group is $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ — while the unpointed one is
  $\operatorname{Out}(G) = \operatorname{Aut}(G)/\operatorname{Inn}(G)$.

---

## 5. The exact price of forgetting

Forgetting the basepoint is now a map between two sets we understand completely,
$$\pi : \operatorname{Hom}(G,H) \;\longrightarrow\; \operatorname{Hom}(G,H)/\text{conjugation},$$
so its fibres are conjugation orbits, and orbit sizes are governed by
[orbit–stabiliser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit%E2%80%93stabilizer_theorem). The
stabiliser of $\varphi$ is the set of $u$ commuting with everything in the image:

> **Fibre-Counting Theorem.** The fibre over the class of a map inducing $\varphi$ has
> exactly
> $$\bigl[\,H : C_H(\varphi(G))\,\bigr]$$
> elements — the index of the centraliser of the image — uniformly in the basepoint.

Two specialisations tell the whole tale:

* $\varphi = \mathrm{id}$: the centraliser is the centre, and the fibre has
  $[G : Z(G)] = |\operatorname{Inn}(G)|$ elements. That is the arithmetic behind
  "$\operatorname{Aut}$ versus $\operatorname{Out}$".
* $H$ abelian: every centraliser is everything, every fibre is a point, and basepoints
  carry no information at all.

## 7. Why anyone should care

* **[Covering spaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covering_space).** Pointed connected
  coverings correspond to subgroups of $\pi_1$; unpointed ones only to *conjugacy classes*
  of subgroups. Same phenomenon, one categorical level down.
* **[Group extensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_extension).** A non-abelian
  extension determines an *outer* action $Q \to \operatorname{Out}(N)$; lifting it to an
  honest action $Q \to \operatorname{Aut}(N)$ is obstructed, and the ambiguity of the lift
  is exactly a fibre of size $[N : Z(N)]$.
* **Gauge theory.** A flat bundle is a holonomy homomorphism up to conjugation; the
  centraliser of the image is the *unbroken symmetry group* of the connection, and the
  index counts the distinct framings.
* **Computation.** Deciding homotopy equivalence, counting homotopy classes and enumerating
  self-equivalences of aspherical complexes all reduce, exactly rather than approximately,
  to finite group computations of the kind above.

---

## 8. Take-away

A basepoint is not decoration; it is a coordinate system. Keep it and the theory is rigid:
classes are homomorphisms, composition is composition, self-equivalences are automorphisms.
Drop it and the theory is flexible but blurred: classes are conjugacy classes, composition
holds up to a conjugator, self-equivalences are outer automorphisms. Between the two sits a
map of finite sets, every one of whose fibres has size the index of a centraliser.

$1$, $3$ and $6$ — go back to the top and watch it happen.

namespace PtdMap

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D] {d : D}

theorem comp_assoc {F : Type u''} [Groupoid.{v''} F] {f : F}

/-- Pointed homotopy classes of pointed self-maps of a 1-type form a monoid under
composition (`x * y` is "first `y`, then `x`"). -/
instance ptdEndMonoid : Monoid (Quotient (ptdSetoid C c C c)) where
  mul x y := compClasses y x
  one := Quotient.mk _ (PtdMap.id C c)
  mul_assoc x y z := by
    induction x using Quotient.ind with
    | _ P =>
      induction y using Quotient.ind with
      | _ Q =>
        induction z using Quotient.ind with
        | _ R => exact Quotient.sound (PtdMap.comp_assoc R Q P).symm
  one_mul x := by
    induction x using Quotient.ind with
    | _ P => exact Quotient.sound (PtdMap.comp_id P)
  mul_one x := by
    induction x using Quotient.ind with
    | _ P => exact Quotient.sound (PtdMap.id_comp P)

theorem ptdEnd_mul_def (x y : Quotient (ptdSetoid C c C c)) : x * y = compClasses y x := rfl

theorem ptdEnd_one_def : (1 : Quotient (ptdSetoid C c C c))
    = Quotient.mk _ (PtdMap.id C c) := rfl

/-- **The monoid of pointed self-maps of a `K(G,1)` is the endomorphism monoid of `G`.**

    Quotient (ptdSetoid C c C c) ≃* Monoid.End (Aut c) where
  toEquiv := ptdClassificationEquiv hC c
  map_mul' x y := by
    induction x using Quotient.ind with
    | _ P =>
      induction y using Quotient.ind with
      | _ Q =>
        show (Q.comp P).ptdHom = _
        exact PtdMap.ptdHom_comp Q P

/-- The units of the endomorphism monoid of a group are its automorphisms. -/
def unitsEndMulEquivMulAut (G : Type*) [Group G] : (Monoid.End G)ˣ ≃* MulAut G where
  toFun u :=
    { toFun := u.val
      invFun := u.inv
      left_inv := fun x => congrArg (fun f : Monoid.End G => f x) u.inv_val
      right_inv := fun x => congrArg (fun f : Monoid.End G => f x) u.val_inv
      map_mul' := fun x y => map_mul u.val x y }
  invFun e :=
    { val := e.toMonoidHom
      inv := e.symm.toMonoidHom
      val_inv := MonoidHom.ext fun x => e.apply_symm_apply x
      inv_val := MonoidHom.ext fun x => e.symm_apply_apply x }
  left_inv _ := Units.ext (MonoidHom.ext fun _ => rfl)
  right_inv _ := MulEquiv.ext fun _ => rfl
  map_mul' _ _ := MulEquiv.ext fun _ => rfl

/-- **The pointed self-homotopy-equivalence group of a `K(G,1)` is `Aut G`.**  This is the
group-level form of `ptdAutEquiv`, and the pointed counterpart of the unpointed theorem
`outAut_mulEquiv_hEnd_units` (`hAut(K(G,1)) ≅ Out G`). -/
noncomputable def ptdAutMulEquiv (hC : ConnectedAt C c) :
    (Quotient (ptdSetoid C c C c))ˣ ≃* MulAut (Aut c) :=
  (Units.mapEquiv (ptdEndMulEquiv hC)).trans (unitsEndMulEquivMulAut (Aut c))

bijective. -/
theorem isUnit_end_iff_bijective {G : Type*} [Group G] (φ : Monoid.End G) :
    IsUnit φ ↔ Function.Bijective φ := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨u, rfl⟩
    exact (unitsEndMulEquivMulAut G u).bijective
  · intro h
    let e := MulEquiv.ofBijective (φ : G →* G) h
    exact ⟨(unitsEndMulEquivMulAut G).symm e, MonoidHom.ext fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- **Pointed Whitehead theorem, monoid form.**  A pointed homotopy class of pointed
self-maps of a connected 1-type is invertible in the monoid of pointed classes exactly when
it is represented by a homotopy equivalence. -/
theorem isUnit_iff_isEquivalence (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (P : PtdMap C c C c) :
    IsUnit (Quotient.mk (ptdSetoid C c C c) P) ↔ P.functor.IsEquivalence := by
  rw [isEquivalence_iff_bijective_ptdHom hC P]

  · intro h
    have h2 : IsUnit ((ptdEndMulEquiv hC) (Quotient.mk (ptdSetoid C c C c) P)) := h.map _
    exact (isUnit_end_iff_bijective _).1 h2
  · intro h
    have h2 : IsUnit ((ptdEndMulEquiv hC) (Quotient.mk (ptdSetoid C c C c) P)) :=
      (isUnit_end_iff_bijective _).2 h
    simpa using h2.map (ptdEndMulEquiv hC).symm

end Monoid

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory
open FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant (ConnectedAt)
open FundamentalGroupK1

namespace FundamentalGroupPointed

universe v u v' u' v'' u''

/-! ## Homotopies with a prescribed value at the basepoint -/

section Intertwiner

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D]

/-- **A homotopy with prescribed value at the basepoint.**  Given an isomorphism `h` at the
basepoint intertwining the two induced actions of the vertex group, there is a natural
isomorphism whose component at the basepoint is exactly `h`.  This refines
`natIso_iff_conjugating_iso`, which only produces *some* natural isomorphism. -/
noncomputable def intertwinerNatIso (hC : ConnectedAt C c) {F G : C ⥤ D}
    (h : F.obj c ≅ G.obj c)
    (hint : ∀ a : Aut c, F.map a.hom ≫ h.hom = h.hom ≫ G.map a.hom) : F ≅ G :=
  NatIso.ofComponents
    (fun X => (F.mapIso (basePath hC X)).symm ≪≫ h ≪≫ G.mapIso (basePath hC X))
    (by
      intro X Y f
      have ha := hint (loopOf hC f)
      rw [loopOf_hom] at ha
      simp only [Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, Functor.mapIso_inv, Functor.mapIso_hom,
        Category.assoc]
      have h1 : F.map f ≫ F.map (basePath hC Y).inv
          = F.map (basePath hC X).inv ≫
              F.map ((basePath hC X).hom ≫ f ≫ (basePath hC Y).inv) := by
        rw [← F.map_comp, ← F.map_comp]
        congr 1
        simp
      have h2 : G.map ((basePath hC X).hom ≫ f ≫ (basePath hC Y).inv) ≫
            G.map (basePath hC Y).hom
          = G.map (basePath hC X).hom ≫ G.map f := by
        rw [← G.map_comp, ← G.map_comp]
        congr 1
        simp
      calc F.map f ≫ F.map (basePath hC Y).inv ≫ h.hom ≫ G.map (basePath hC Y).hom
          = (F.map f ≫ F.map (basePath hC Y).inv) ≫ h.hom ≫ G.map (basePath hC Y).hom := by
            simp
        _ = F.map (basePath hC X).inv ≫ (F.map ((basePath hC X).hom ≫ f ≫ (basePath hC Y).inv)
              ≫ h.hom) ≫ G.map (basePath hC Y).hom := by rw [h1]; simp
        _ = F.map (basePath hC X).inv ≫
              (h.hom ≫ G.map ((basePath hC X).hom ≫ f ≫ (basePath hC Y).inv))
              ≫ G.map (basePath hC Y).hom := by rw [ha]
        _ = F.map (basePath hC X).inv ≫ h.hom ≫ G.map (basePath hC X).hom ≫ G.map f := by
            rw [Category.assoc, h2])

@[simp] theorem intertwinerNatIso_app (hC : ConnectedAt C c) {F G : C ⥤ D}
    (h : F.obj c ≅ G.obj c)
    (hint : ∀ a : Aut c, F.map a.hom ≫ h.hom = h.hom ≫ G.map a.hom) :
    (intertwinerNatIso hC h hint).hom.app c = h.hom := by
  simp [intertwinerNatIso]

end Intertwiner

/-! ## Pointed maps of 1-types -/

/-- A **pointed map** of 1-types: a functor together with a chosen path (isomorphism) from
the image of the source basepoint to the target basepoint. -/
structure PtdMap (C : Type u) [Groupoid.{v} C] (c : C)
    (D : Type u') [Groupoid.{v'} D] (d : D) where
  /-- The underlying map of 1-types. -/
  functor : C ⥤ D
  /-- The chosen path identifying the image of the basepoint with the basepoint. -/
  path : functor.obj c ≅ d

namespace PtdMap

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D] {d : D}

/-- The homomorphism of fundamental groups induced by a pointed map.  Unlike the unpointed
`inducedHom`, no choice of path is involved. -/
def ptdHom (P : PtdMap C c D d) : Aut c →* Aut d :=
  (Aut.autMulEquivOfIso P.path).toMonoidHom.comp (P.functor.mapAut c)

theorem ptdHom_hom (P : PtdMap C c D d) (a : Aut c) :
    (P.ptdHom a).hom = P.path.inv ≫ P.functor.map a.hom ≫ P.path.hom := rfl

/-- **Pointed homotopy**: a natural isomorphism compatible with the chosen paths. -/
def PtdHomotopic (P Q : PtdMap C c D d) : Prop :=
  ∃ α : P.functor ≅ Q.functor, α.hom.app c ≫ Q.path.hom = P.path.hom

theorem PtdHomotopic.refl (P : PtdMap C c D d) : PtdHomotopic P P :=
  ⟨Iso.refl _, by simp⟩

theorem PtdHomotopic.symm {P Q : PtdMap C c D d} (h : PtdHomotopic P Q) : PtdHomotopic Q P := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
  refine ⟨α.symm, ?_⟩
  rw [← hα]
  simp

theorem PtdHomotopic.trans {P Q R : PtdMap C c D d} (h : PtdHomotopic P Q)
    (h' : PtdHomotopic Q R) : PtdHomotopic P R := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨β, hβ⟩ := h'
  refine ⟨α ≪≫ β, ?_⟩
  rw [← hα, ← hβ]
  simp

/-- Pointed homotopy is an equivalence relation; the quotient is the set of pointed homotopy
classes of maps `(C,c) → (D,d)`. -/
def ptdSetoid (C : Type u) [Groupoid.{v} C] (c : C)
    (D : Type u') [Groupoid.{v'} D] (d : D) : Setoid (PtdMap C c D d) where
  r := PtdHomotopic
  iseqv := ⟨PtdHomotopic.refl, PtdHomotopic.symm, PtdHomotopic.trans⟩

/-- **Pointed homotopies do not change the induced homomorphism** — not even up to
conjugation. -/
theorem ptdHom_congr {P Q : PtdMap C c D d} (h : PtdHomotopic P Q) : P.ptdHom = Q.ptdHom := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
  have hinv : P.path.inv = Q.path.inv ≫ α.inv.app c := by
    apply Iso.inv_ext
    rw [← hα]
    simp
  ext a
  rw [ptdHom_hom, ptdHom_hom, hinv, ← hα]
  have hnat : P.functor.map a.hom ≫ α.hom.app c = α.hom.app c ≫ Q.functor.map a.hom :=
    α.hom.naturality a.hom
  simp only [Category.assoc]
  rw [← Category.assoc (P.functor.map a.hom), hnat]
  simp

/-- **Conversely, the induced homomorphism is a complete invariant of the pointed homotopy
class** (for a connected source). -/
theorem ptdHomotopic_of_ptdHom_eq (hC : ConnectedAt C c) {P Q : PtdMap C c D d}
    (h : P.ptdHom = Q.ptdHom) : PtdHomotopic P Q := by
  have key : ∀ a : Aut c,
      P.functor.map a.hom ≫ (P.path ≪≫ Q.path.symm).hom
        = (P.path ≪≫ Q.path.symm).hom ≫ Q.functor.map a.hom := by
    intro a
    have ha : P.path.inv ≫ P.functor.map a.hom ≫ P.path.hom
        = Q.path.inv ≫ Q.functor.map a.hom ≫ Q.path.hom := by
      rw [← ptdHom_hom, ← ptdHom_hom, h]
    have ha' : P.functor.map a.hom ≫ P.path.hom
        = P.path.hom ≫ Q.path.inv ≫ Q.functor.map a.hom ≫ Q.path.hom := by
      rw [← ha]
      simp
    simp only [Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom]
    rw [← Category.assoc, ha']
    simp
  refine ⟨intertwinerNatIso hC (P.path ≪≫ Q.path.symm) key, ?_⟩
  rw [intertwinerNatIso_app]
  simp

end PtdMap

/-! ## The pointed classification -/

section Classification

open PtdMap

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D]

/-- The canonical pointed realization of a homomorphism of fundamental groups. -/
noncomputable def ptdRealize (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d : D) (φ : Aut c →* Aut d) :
    PtdMap C c D d :=
  ⟨realize hC d φ, Iso.refl d⟩

@[simp] theorem ptdHom_ptdRealize (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d : D) (φ : Aut c →* Aut d) :
    (ptdRealize hC d φ).ptdHom = φ := by
  ext a
  rw [ptdHom_hom]
  show 𝟙 d ≫ (realize hC d φ).map a.hom ≫ 𝟙 d = (φ a).hom
  rw [realize_map_aut]
  simp

/-- **The pointed classification of maps of 1-types.**  Pointed homotopy classes of pointed
maps `(K(G,1),*) → (K(H,1),*)` are in bijection with `Hom(G,H)` itself — no quotient by
conjugation.  Compare `classificationEquiv`, where the unpointed classes are only in
bijection with `Hom(G,H)/conj`. -/
noncomputable def ptdClassificationEquiv (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d : D) :
    Quotient (ptdSetoid C c D d) ≃ (Aut c →* Aut d) where
  toFun := Quotient.lift PtdMap.ptdHom fun _ _ h => ptdHom_congr h
  invFun φ := Quotient.mk _ (ptdRealize hC d φ)
  left_inv x := by
    induction x using Quotient.ind with
    | _ P =>
      refine Quotient.sound (ptdHomotopic_of_ptdHom_eq hC ?_).symm
      exact (ptdHom_ptdRealize hC d P.ptdHom).symm
  right_inv φ := ptdHom_ptdRealize hC d φ

@[simp] theorem ptdClassificationEquiv_mk (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d : D)
    (P : PtdMap C c D d) :
    ptdClassificationEquiv hC d (Quotient.mk _ P) = P.ptdHom := rfl

end Classification

/-! ## Strict functoriality of the pointed classification -/

namespace PtdMap

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D] {d : D}
  {E : Type u''} [Groupoid.{v''} E] {e : E}

/-- The identity pointed map. -/
def id (C : Type u) [Groupoid.{v} C] (c : C) : PtdMap C c C c := ⟨𝟭 C, Iso.refl c⟩

/-- Composition of pointed maps. -/
def comp (P : PtdMap C c D d) (Q : PtdMap D d E e) : PtdMap C c E e :=
  ⟨P.functor ⋙ Q.functor, Q.functor.mapIso P.path ≪≫ Q.path⟩

/-- **The identity map induces the identity homomorphism.**  Compare `inducedHom_id`. -/
@[simp] theorem ptdHom_id : (PtdMap.id C c).ptdHom = MonoidHom.id (Aut c) := by
  ext a
  rw [ptdHom_hom]
  show 𝟙 c ≫ a.hom ≫ 𝟙 c = a.hom
  simp

/-- **The pointed classification is strictly functorial**: the homomorphism induced by a
composite of pointed maps is *equal* to the composite of the induced homomorphisms.  This is
the pointed refinement of `inducedHom_comp_conj`, where the corresponding statement holds
only up to conjugation. -/
theorem ptdHom_comp (P : PtdMap C c D d) (Q : PtdMap D d E e) :
    (P.comp Q).ptdHom = Q.ptdHom.comp P.ptdHom := by
  ext a
  rw [ptdHom_hom]
  show (Q.functor.mapIso P.path ≪≫ Q.path).inv ≫ Q.functor.map (P.functor.map a.hom) ≫
      (Q.functor.mapIso P.path ≪≫ Q.path).hom = _
  rw [MonoidHom.comp_apply, ptdHom_hom, ptdHom_hom]
  simp only [Iso.trans_hom, Iso.trans_inv, Functor.mapIso_hom, Functor.mapIso_inv,
    Q.functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]

/-- Composition of pointed maps is compatible with pointed homotopy, so it descends to
pointed homotopy classes. -/
theorem PtdHomotopic.comp {P P' : PtdMap C c D d} {Q Q' : PtdMap D d E e}
    (h : PtdHomotopic P P') (h' : PtdHomotopic Q Q') :
    PtdHomotopic (P.comp Q) (P'.comp Q') := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨β, hβ⟩ := h'
  refine ⟨Functor.isoWhiskerRight α Q.functor ≪≫ Functor.isoWhiskerLeft P'.functor β, ?_⟩
  show (Q.functor.map (α.hom.app c) ≫ β.hom.app (P'.functor.obj c)) ≫
      (Q'.functor.mapIso P'.path ≪≫ Q'.path).hom = (Q.functor.mapIso P.path ≪≫ Q.path).hom
  have hnat : β.hom.app (P'.functor.obj c) ≫ Q'.functor.map P'.path.hom
      = Q.functor.map P'.path.hom ≫ β.hom.app d := (β.hom.naturality P'.path.hom).symm
  simp only [Iso.trans_hom, Functor.mapIso_hom, Category.assoc]
  rw [← Category.assoc (β.hom.app (P'.functor.obj c)), hnat, Category.assoc, hβ,
    ← Category.assoc, ← Q.functor.map_comp, hα]

/-- Composition of pointed homotopy classes. -/
def compClasses : Quotient (ptdSetoid C c D d) → Quotient (ptdSetoid D d E e) →
    Quotient (ptdSetoid C c E e) :=
  Quotient.map₂ PtdMap.comp fun _ _ h _ _ h' => PtdHomotopic.comp h h'
